comparator.name: Interdisciplinary Social Science (Interdisciplinaire sociale wetenschap)
comparator.academicYear: Current UvA published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 contains 60 EC of disciplinary introductions, methods and integration practica. Year 2 contains 36 EC specified theory, qualitative and quantitative methods and policy research plus a genuine 24-EC restricted choice of interdisciplinary thematic modules. Year 3 has 9 EC philosophy of interdisciplinary research, a 9-EC deepening-module choice, 30 EC minor/elective space and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The broad interdisciplinary literature-study option is selected for the 9-EC deepening choice without combining mutually exclusive alternatives. UCR has no comparable compulsory five-discipline practicum structure or dedicated cultural anthropology and human-geography sequence.

alternatives.label: Social science, behaviour and public challenges
alternatives.concept: Integrates sociology, politics, psychology, empirical methods, policy and civic research to address social problems. It is the closest feasible UCR response to the UvA programme, while UCR lacks its dedicated anthropology, human geography and compulsory integration-practicum sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed courses combine sociological, political and psychological study with qualitative and quantitative methods, policy and collective challenges.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede their dependent courses and all planned terms are available. Foundation courses in sociology, psychology, politics and methods precede advanced theory, policy, research and health study; nine 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Inequality, rights and public policy
alternatives.concept: Uses the programme’s explicit inequality and inclusion focus to organise sociology, political institutions, law, historical gender analysis, rights and public economics around the distribution of power and policy responses.
alternatives.labelReason: The final course set gives sustained weight to social inequality, rights, constitutional and EU institutions, historical gender experience and redistribution.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest response, this route replaces the psychological foundation and advanced psychological research sequence with Histories of Gender, Political Philosophy, Human Rights, Comparative Constitutional Law and EU Law. The shift exceeds 30 EC and changes both its methods and its central policy questions.
progression: All formal law and economics prerequisites precede dependent courses, planned offerings cover every assignment and 300-level work follows introductory sociology, politics, methods and law. Eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Health, behaviour and social policy
alternatives.concept: Develops the UvA programme’s named Health theme by connecting sociological and political analysis with psychology, public health, research synthesis and economic policy. It treats health as a social and behavioural question without claiming to reproduce a medical degree.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum pairs core social science and research with epidemiology, health psychology, emotion, and clinical psychology.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to both preceding programmes, the curriculum adds a life-science foundation, epidemiology, medical and health psychology, psychodiagnostics and quantitative causal analysis. These replace substantial law, political and media courses; each pair differs by at least 30 EC and the health strand determines the educational choice.
progression: The psychology and life-science gateways precede advanced psychology and immunology; research methods precede advanced evidence synthesis and econometrics. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; ten 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The broad social-science response is the closest feasible UCR composition. The official curriculum and exact-target interests also support distinct inequality-and-policy and health-and-society directions. Each is academically coherent, feasible in the current UCR catalogue and differs from both others by at least four courses (30 EC), so production stops at three.

blocks: Both introduce sociological explanations of social inequality, cohesion and culture.
Both teach qualitative social-research design, interpretation and an applied research project.
Both develop theories of social action and structure, although the UvA module is broader and twice the credit value.
Both connect social theory with an empirical project involving civil-society or policy concerns, though the UvA component explicitly focuses on policy research.
Both examine social influences on individual and group behaviour, while the UvA module also introduces broader psychology.
Both teach quantitative and statistical research methods for behavioural or social data, with differing scope.
The UvA introductory interdisciplinary social-issues module has no single selected UCR course with its five-discipline integration function.
The UvA inclusion practicum combines external-client and interdisciplinary project work that no single selected UCR course reproduces.
UCR has no selected cultural-anthropology course with this module’s ethnographic and theoretical focus.
No selected UCR course directly teaches this human-geography and urban-space curriculum.
Both introduce political institutions and compare political systems, although the UvA course also connects several social sciences.
Both develop initial academic reading, writing, reflection and participation skills, though the UvA practicum has a different credit weight.
Both teach research questions, study design, data collection and initial quantitative analysis, with different disciplinary framing.
The second UvA academic-skills practicum has a distinct supervised integration function beyond the single UCR PPD course.
The philosophy of inter- and transdisciplinary research has no direct selected UCR counterpart.
The selected 9-EC interdisciplinary literature-study module has no directly equivalent selected UCR component.
The independent bachelor thesis is not a scheduled UCR course; the standard optional-research comparison element is placed here.
Both examine practical sustainability governance across public and civic actors; UCR does not reproduce the UvA group practicum.
The restricted 24-EC thematic choice remains an open selection; assigning it to one UCR course would imply an unchosen theme.
The 30-EC minor/elective space is genuinely open and cannot be represented by one UCR course.

notes.text: The UvA programme integrates sociology, psychology, politics, cultural anthropology and human geography through compulsory research methods and repeated externally engaged practica. UCR can combine substantial social theory, politics, psychology, research, policy, health and sustainability study, but it does not reproduce the same five-discipline foundation, anthropology and human-geography depth, or compulsory integration-practicum sequence.
